text:
olivia: quick heads-up — a customer using the new edge sample (vite + next-edge) hit a crash during deploy: `TypeError: Cannot read property 'create' of undefined` referencing our SDK. stack points to `.default` vs named import mismatch. anyone able to explain why this keeps happening?

raj: i've seen this with Vite + esbuild. root cause is usually the consumer bundling expecting a default export but our package surfaced CJS shape at runtime (module.exports = { createClient }) so the bundler ends up with an object with no `.default`.

trina: also depends on TS settings. if you compile with `esModuleInterop:false` and `allowSyntheticDefaultImports:false`, `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` can compile differently. most users don't set these flags and then their bundler/runtime behavior diverges.

ben: practical troubleshooting steps i tell users: try `import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` or switch to `const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')` in node. for edge/Vite, `import * as` is usually safer. but we should document it.

olivia: customer is using plain JS with Vite (no TS), so tsconfig flags won't help them. they expect the package to work with `import Redwood from`. what can we change in the package to make that reliable?

raj: package.json `exports` map is critical. We can add explicit ESM entry that re-exports the default. e.g., in esm build add `export { default } from './index.js'` so bundlers that look for a default will find it. also ensure `package.json` keeps an explicit `main` for CJS and `module`/`exports` for ESM.

trina: small note: some edge deployers (Netlify, Cloudflare) run additional transformations — they might rewrite import forms and inadvertently strip wrappers. not much we can do there other than documenting common gotchas.

ben: can we add a tiny runtime compatibility shim? something like at top of CJS build: `module.exports = module.exports.default || module.exports` so if someone imports the CJS version as a namespace it still has `.default`.

raj: yes, or add an index.cjs that sets `exports.default = exports` for safety. But be careful with circular references and size. keep it minimal.

docs-bot: FYI we already have a page but it only lists "ESM vs CJS" high level. missing: bundle-specific fixes (Vite/esbuild), tsconfig snippets, and a code sample showing a defensive import pattern.

olivia: OK plan: 1) docs PR with a short matrix: bundler/runtime -> recommended import pattern -> minimal fix (tsconfig or bundler config). 2) small SDK patch to adjust exports/shim and add a CI smoke test that bundles quickstart with Vite and runs on a node-based edge shim. 3) link the repro to the PR.

trina: for the docs sample, suggest adding this snippet (works in most cases):
```js
// safest cross-bundler import (JS/TS)
import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const Client = ('default' in Redwood) ? Redwood.default : Redwood
const client = Client.createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY })
```

ben: i'd rather prefer a typed TS example for users who use TS: show tsconfig and `import Redwood from` when `esModuleInterop` is enabled.

olina: (typo: olivia) we should probably include both. short table + two code snippets (JS safe import, TS recommended tsconfig). keep it tiny so it fits in quickstart.

raj: i'll open a tiny PR to the SDK repo to change package exports and add `exports.default` shim. will add a unit test that imports both ESM and CJS consumers (node + esbuild).

docs-bot: Suggested doc copy: 
- "If you see runtime errors referencing .default or createClient undefined, try `import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` or enable `esModuleInterop` in TypeScript. See examples below."

olivia: please tag me on both PRs and paste any repro links here. i'll coordinate a docs + SDK release note. thanks all :white_check_mark:
